record.original_question: Let c(n) and b(n) denote respectively the numbers of central and bicentral unlabeled n-vertex trees. Determine whether c(n)/b(n) tends to 1 as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE: Let c(n) and b(n) be the numbers of central and bicentral unlabeled n-vertex trees, respectively. Then c(n)/b(n) → 1 as n → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A tree is a finite connected acyclic simple graph. The eccentricity of a vertex v in a tree T is the maximum distance from v to any other vertex of T. The center of T is the set of vertices of minimum eccentricity; it is a classical theorem that the center of a tree consists of either exactly one vertex or two adjacent vertices. A tree is called central if its center has exactly one vertex, and bicentral if its center has exactly two vertices. Two trees are considered the same as unlabeled trees if they are isomorphic as graphs.

For each positive integer n, let c(n) denote the number of central unlabeled trees on n vertices and let b(n) denote the number of bicentral unlabeled trees on n vertices.

Determine whether
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c(n)}{b(n)}=1.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the OEIS sequences A000676 (central unlabeled trees) and A000677 (bicentral unlabeled trees) and standard asymptotics of unlabeled trees (Otter), but no source was found that explicitly establishes or refutes the conjecture c(n)/b(n) → 1. The status could not be conclusively determined from public sources.

status_evidence.title: A000676 - OEIS (centered trees)
status_evidence.snippet: Number of centered trees with n nodes.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the central (centered) unlabeled tree counts c(n).

status_evidence.title: Centered/Bicentered Tree - Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: A bicentered tree is a tree having two graph centers; a centered tree has a single center.
status_evidence.claim: Provides standard definitions of central vs bicentral trees underlying the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A000055 - OEIS (number of trees with n unlabeled nodes)
status_evidence.snippet: Total unlabeled trees a(n) = A000676(n) + A000677(n).
status_evidence.claim: Confirms partition of unlabeled trees into central and bicentral classes; no asymptotic ratio result is recorded.
